stated_limitation: The low proportion of identified place cells reflects the conservative thresholds used and the fact that granule cells (targeted in this dataset) are generally less selective than CA1 pyramidal neurons.

justification.dataset: A Buzsaki-lab hippocampal dataset that does contain place cells, but the granule-cell emphasis, 23 units, and tiny covered arena make the demonstration harder than it needed to be.
justification.handling: Real data is streamed and spikes are correctly aligned to position, but there is no unit quality filtering and the occupancy mask is very lenient, yielding sparse noisy maps.
justification.analysis: The Skaggs spatial-information formula is miscomputed (unweighted mean instead of occupancy-weighted mean), sparsity is nonstandard, and there is no shuffle/null control behind the threshold-based place-cell calls.
justification.correctness: The buggy normalization produces negative spatial information (to -5.5 bits/spike), which is physically impossible and is presented as a finding, capping this axis at 0.
justification.figures: The statistics panels are readable but the place-field maps are noisy, low-rate (~2 Hz) blobs over a tiny region that do not show the clear localized fields the text claims.
justification.honesty: It presents a demonstrably broken SI statistic (negative values) as a real finding and describes noisy weak maps as clear place fields, both disqualifying acts.
justification.verdict: A physically impossible headline statistic presented as a finding, a broken analysis, and overstated figures make this a start-over.
